children: Solvay is in talks with One Investment Management over a potential strategic partnership for its rare-earth business.
The Belgian chemical group said Tuesday that there could be no certainty at this stage that the discussions would result in any agreement or transaction.
Rare-earth minerals are critical for high-tech industries such as electronics, defense and the energy transition, and Western countries are seeking to boost capacity and curb their reliance on China.
Solvay's rare-earth business is focused on rare-earth separation, recycling, purification and formulation and includes a specialty production site in La Rochelle, France.
The talks follow recent investments in the industry by One Investment Management.

Last year, it participated in a $65 million investment in Durham, N.C.-based Vulcan Elements, which produces neodymium iron boron magnets used in defense and commercial products, and early this year it invested $200 million in Texas-based Noveon Magnetics, a maker of NdFeB magnets that uses recycled materials in the manufacturing process.
